newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. China envoy sees U.S. pressing human rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. China envoy sees U.S. pressing human rights.

text.p: James Sasser, the U.S. ambassador to China, said on Thursday he expects Washington to ask the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva to adopt a resolution criticising China for human rights abuses.

Sasser, accompanying U.S. Vice-President Al Gore on his visit to China, indicated that both the United States and China were somewhat resigned to what has become an annual struggle before the U.N. body.
The United States will "probably move forward" with the resolution, Sasser said, adding: "We're both sort of locked into a Greek tragedy situation in Geneva."
He complained that other countries, including France and Germany, offer only limited support in the fight for the resolution. "Everybody else will sort of hold our coat," he said.
Gore on Wednesday concluded two days of talks with Chinese leaders on a broad range of issues, including human rights.
